title: An $\ell$-adic realization of algebraic numbers exists and fixes the rationals
statement:
Fix a prime $p$, $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\Fq$, $k=\Fbar$, and a prime $\ell\neq p$; write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ of $\mathbf Q$ and let

$$
\overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell)}=\{z\in\Qlb:z\text{ is algebraic over }\mathbf Q\}
$$

be the algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q$ inside $\Qlb$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure-q]. Then $\overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell)}$ is an algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q$: it is an algebraically closed field and every element of it is algebraic over $\mathbf Q$. Consequently there exists a $\mathbf Q$-isomorphism

$$
\jmath:\overline{\mathbf Q}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\overline{\mathbf Q}^{(\ell)},
$$

that is, an $\ell$-adic realization of algebraic numbers in the sense of [def-weil-algebraic-closure-q] exists. Every such $\jmath$ is the identity on $\mathbf Q$, hence sends every integer $c$ to $c\cdot1_{\Qlb}$.
